cleanIntro: The RAK-47 is a US-made AK-pattern rifle and it strips the way an AK does: dust cover, recoil spring, carrier and bolt, then the gas tube off the rear sight. ⚠ Two things catch people. The recoil spring guide is what RETAINS the dust cover — press it in before you lift — and the gas tube comes off by rotating a LOCK LEVER on the rear sight, not by pulling. Riley's own closing instruction is a thin coat of gun oil and a clean bore after EVERY use.

steps.title: Magazine out, handle fully back, chamber AND receiver inspected
steps.action: Remove the magazine and pull the charging/operating handle fully to the rear. Inspect the chamber AND the receiver to make sure no cartridges are present, then release the operating handle.
steps.prose: An AK has no bolt hold-open, so this is a hold-it-yourself-and-look step. Riley asks for both the chamber and the receiver.
steps.quote:
1. Remove the magazine and pull the charging/operating handle fully to the rear. Inspect the 
chamber and receiver to ensure no cartridges are present.
steps.cite: RAK 47 OWNER MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — Disassembly, step 1, p.7

steps.title: ⚠ Press the SPRING GUIDE in before the dust cover will lift
steps.action: Press the serrated end of the driving spring guide INTO the bolt cover, and while you hold it in, lift the cover off REAR END FIRST. The spring guide is the retainer — the cover is not clipped on, it is held by that protruding tip.
steps.prose: Trying to prise the cover off without pressing the guide is how covers get bent, and it is the commonest AK mistake.
steps.caution: Rear end first. The front of the cover sits in a channel behind the rear sight.
steps.quote:
Press the serrated end of the driving spring guide (figure 02) into the bolt cover, and while 
holding the guide in, lift off the bolt cover, rear end first (figure 03).
steps.cite: RAK 47 OWNER MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — Disassembly, step 2, p.7

steps.title: Recoil spring: push FORWARD to unhook it from the stock tang
steps.action: Push forward on the end of the spring guide to disengage it from its base in the rear stock tang, then pull the complete spring assembly out of the bolt carrier. Forward first, then out — it does not simply lift.
steps.prose: That base is a slot in the receiver tang. Forward clears the hook; anything else fights it.
steps.quote:
Push forward on the end of the spring guide disengaging it from its base (rear stock tang figure 
04); then pull the complete spring assembly out of the bolt carrier.
steps.cite: RAK 47 OWNER MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — Disassembly, step 3, p.7

steps.title: Carrier and bolt out — back, lift, then off
steps.action: Pull the charging handle fully to the rear, lift the bolt carrier slightly UPWARD, and remove the bolt and carrier together. The rails only release at the very back of the travel.
steps.prose: Slightly upward is the whole trick. Straight back stops against the rails.
steps.quote:
Pull the charging handle fully to the rear (figure 05), lift the bolt carrier slightly upward and then         
remove the bolt and carrier.
steps.cite: RAK 47 OWNER MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — Disassembly, step 4, p.8

steps.title: Bolt out of the carrier — press IN, twist, then straight forward
steps.action: Press the bolt INTO the carrier until the bolt operating lug can be twisted free of its cam track, then pull the bolt straight forward and out. It is a cam, so it has to be pushed back before it will rotate.
steps.prose: In, then twist, then forward. Pulling first jams the lug against the cam.
steps.quote:
Press the bolt into the carrier until the bolt operating lug can be twisted free of its cam in the 
carrier (figure 06). Pull the bolt straight forward and out of the carrier.
steps.cite: RAK 47 OWNER MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — Disassembly, step 5, p.8

steps.title: Gas tube: rotate the LOCK LEVER up on the rear sight
steps.action: Rotate the gas cylinder tube lock lever UPWARD on the rear sight to free the tube, then pull up on the rear of the hand guard and take the tube off. ⛔ The lever is the whole retention — never lever the tube out without turning it first.
steps.prose: That lever is stiff on a new rifle and it is meant to be. A cartridge rim is the traditional tool.
steps.quote:
Rotate the gas cylinder tube lock lever upward on the rear sight (figure 07) to free the gas 
cylinder tube. Pull up on the rear of the hand guard and remove the tube.
steps.cite: RAK 47 OWNER MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — Disassembly, step 6, p.8

steps.title: ⛔ Thin coat of gun oil and a clean bore AFTER EVERY USE
steps.action: Riley's stated maintenance for this rifle is short and it is a habit, not a schedule: apply a thin coat of gun oil and clean the bore after each use, to extend the life of the rifle. On a rifle that is often fed corrosive surplus ammunition, the bore half of that is not optional.
steps.prose: One sentence, and it is the closing line of the manual — placed where you finish reassembling.
steps.quote: To extend the life of your rifle always apply a thin coat of gun oil and clean the bore after each use!
steps.cite: RAK 47 OWNER MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — Reassembly, closing line, p.10

steps.title: Gas tube back FIRST — front to the block, then the lock lever down
steps.action: Mate the FRONT of the tube to the gas block, push the tube down so the bottom lip drops into the notch in the rear sight, then rotate the lock lever COUNTER-CLOCKWISE until it seats in the indentation on the rear sight. If the lever will not seat, the lip is not in the notch.
steps.prose: Front, down, lever. A lever that turns easily but does not seat means the tube is a millimetre proud.
steps.quote:
Install the gas tube by mating the front of the tube to the gas block, then push the tube  
down with the bottom lip on the tube into the notch in the rear sight, then rotate the lock 
lever counter clock wise until it is seated in the indentation on the rear sight.
steps.cite: RAK 47 OWNER MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — Reassembly, step 1, p.10

steps.title: Bolt into carrier, twist and pull FORWARD to its stop
steps.action: Install the bolt head into the bolt carrier, then twist the bolt and pull it forward until it stops. ⛔ It must be left in that forward position for the carrier to go back into the receiver — that is the next step's precondition.
steps.prose: A bolt left back in the carrier will not let the group drop onto the rails.
steps.quote:
Install the bolt head into the bolt carrier, then twist the bolt and pull forward until the bolt 
stops.
steps.cite: RAK 47 OWNER MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — Reassembly, step 2, p.10

steps.title: Carrier in: piston into the rear sight area, tilt down onto the rails
steps.action: With the bolt head pulled FORWARD in the carrier, put the gas piston into the rear sight area, tilt the carrier down into the rear slots on the receiver, and push it forward into place.
steps.prose: Piston first, then tilt. Trying to land the rails before the piston is in the tube never works.
steps.quote:
With the bolt head pulled forward in the carrier, put the gas piston into the rear sight area, 
tilt the carrier down and into the rear slots on the receiver and push forward into place.
steps.cite: RAK 47 OWNER MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — Reassembly, step 3, p.10

steps.title: Spring in the carrier's top hole, then the dust cover front-edge first
steps.action: Install the recoil spring into the TOP hole on the carrier, press the spring in and place the recoil push button into the stock tang. Then the cover: front edge into the U-shaped channel behind the rear sight, and push the REAR down while still pressing TOWARD the rear sight so the front edge does not unseat.
steps.prose: Two hands, two directions. Let the forward pressure off and the front edge hops out every time.
steps.quote:
Install the front edge of the cover into the mating U shaped channel on the back of the rear 
sight and push the rear of the cover downwards and while still applying pressure towards 
the rear sight so that the front edge of the dust cover doesn’t unseat itself from the U 
shaped channel.
steps.cite: RAK 47 OWNER MANUAL — SEPTEMBER 2016 — Reassembly, step 5, p.10

deepAbsentReason: Riley Defense's RAK 47 manual publishes a full field strip and a full reassembly and NOTHING BEYOND IT. There is no trigger-group removal, no barrel or gas-block work, no solvent or interval guidance, and no cleaning section of its own — the only maintenance sentence in the document is the closing line, 'To extend the life of your rifle always apply a thin coat of gun oil and clean the bore after each use!', which is carried in the routine steps above. Nothing deeper is published for this rifle, so nothing deeper is written here. This listing therefore has NO deep clean.

cleaning.name: AFTER EVERY USE — RILEY'S OWN INSTRUCTION
tasks: Thin coat of gun oil on the rifle

cleaning.name: WHILE IT IS APART
tasks: Bolt face, lug and cam track wiped
Carrier rails and gas piston wiped
Gas tube interior and the rear-sight notch cleared of carbon
Recoil spring and guide wiped and lightly oiled

reassembly: Gas tube: front to the gas block, lip into the rear-sight notch, lock lever counter-clockwise until seated.
Bolt into the carrier, twisted and pulled FORWARD to its stop.
Piston into the rear sight area, carrier tilted down into the rear slots, pushed forward.
Recoil spring into the TOP hole of the carrier; push button into the stock tang.
Dust cover front edge into the U-channel, rear pressed down with forward pressure held.
Charging handle cycled and released to check function.
Selector lever turned counter-clockwise to SAFE.
fncheck: Riley's own two closing steps, in order: pull the charging handle backwards and release it to check for function, then turn the selector lever counter-clockwise to the safe position. ⚠ Before that, confirm the gas tube lock lever is fully seated in its indentation on the rear sight and that the dust cover's front edge is still in the U-channel — a cover that is proud at the front will lift under recoil.
